title: Short Stuff: Most Haunted House in England
summary: Short Stuff Halloween episode on Borley Rectory, a rectory in Borley, Essex, England, long reputed to be the most haunted house in England. Covers the site's monastery-era legends (a headless monk, a walled-up nun), the Reverend Henry Bull family who built the rectory in 1862 and reported hauntings, the Foister family, the 1939 fire blamed on flying books and a paraffin lamp, paranormal investigator Harry Price's year-long study and his books, the later SPR debunking that implicated Mary Ann Foister in hoaxes, and a 2000 memoir by a purported former resident, Louis Marsland, whose existence could not be verified. The hosts also joke about a few non-topical tangents.

segments.title: Halloween intro and Borley Rectory setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the Halloween Short Stuff, referencing an earlier Halloween episode, then introduce Borley Rectory as the most haunted house in England and explain what a rectory is.

segments.title: Monastery legends and Bull family arrival
segments.summary: The hosts describe the site's older legends, including a headless monk and a walled-up nun tied to a monastery, and a later nun who was strangled and buried in a cellar. The Reverend Henry Bull built the rectory in 1862, and reported phenomena included bells, keys flying from locks, and a phantom stagecoach.

segments.title: Harry Price and his investigation
segments.summary: Harry Price, a well-known paranormal investigator and debunker of mediums, was sent by the Daily Mail to Borley Rectory and concluded it was haunted, lending credibility to the claims. The hosts also describe his feud with the Society for Psychical Research and his founding of his own laboratory.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Brief break before returning to the rectory story.

segments.title: 1939 fire and Price's year-long study
segments.summary: The house burned in 1939; owner William Gregson said books flew off a shelf and knocked over a paraffin lamp. Harry Price had leased the house for a year with assistants to study the phenomena, and his books, including The Most Haunted House in England, cemented its reputation.
topics: The Most Haunted House in England

segments.title: Debunking and hoax revelations
segments.summary: The Society for Psychical Research researchers later challenged Price's work, finding in his unpublished notes that Mary Ann Foister was central to hoaxes, and suggesting Price himself threw pebbles during seances. A 2000 memoir by a purported former resident, Louis Marsland, described hoaxes and an unexplained bell event, but researchers could find no record of a person by that name living there.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up the Halloween episode and note the Stuff You Should Know production credit.
